question: On realistic long-horizon legal work, what retrieval surface best preserves task quality while reducing context and tool failure cost when the model, authoring tools, progressive disclosure policy, and tasks are held constant?

corpus.selection_rule: Include every eligible visible genre once, then round-robin seeded candidates across practice areas. Require docx, md, or txt deliverables and at most 40 task files.

arms.p0: Strict coding retrieval: Glob, Grep, and line-window Read. No structural handles in Read, Edit, or prompt prose.
arms.d1: Routed coding retrieval: Glob, Grep, and Read plus verified legal structural handles for bounded reads and edits.
arms.address: Project-native retrieval: library outline, find, read, links, page/provision/table addresses, and graph following.

execution.launch_gate: All three smoke arms must finish, emit a surface receipt, have zero implementation-level tool failures, and produce an evaluator-readable deliverable.
execution.paired_order: All three arms run concurrently per task; task order is the registered list.
execution.failure_policy: Retain failed cells in operational metrics, never score missing output as a successful task, diagnose implementation failures separately, and do not replace tasks after score inspection.

outcomes.judge: Use the native LAB evaluator with codex/gpt-5.6-luna first. Scores are derivative LLM-judge labels, not human gold; calibrate a fixed subset with Claude before a winner claim.
outcomes.decision_rule: No arm is selected from token savings alone. Prefer the leanest arm whose paired task quality is not materially worse; if d1 preserves p0 efficiency while improving structure-heavy tasks, carry d1 forward as the hybrid base. Address must earn its extra calls and context on structure-sensitive criteria.
